necessary.observation: Continuation checkpoints store config/optimizer/RNG/usage but do not bind the training implementation/revision. necessary.observation: When SIGALRM/alarm are unavailable, the driver writes job-origin and creates .formal-running, catches the first AttributeError, then finally calls missing signal.alarm again. That second AttributeError prevents job-result persistence and lock removal. A labeled private audit fixture exercised the actual checked_job gate before this failure; no training function was invoked.
necessary.impact: Unsupported platforms such as Windows are not safely rejected before attempt mutation and can be left with a stale global lock plus no failure receipt.
necessary.required: Either implement a real portable hard-deadline mechanism or explicitly reject unsupported alarm capability before creating attempt directories/locks. Cleanup/error persistence must not themselves call unavailable APIs; do not silently remove the deadline.

necessary.observation: A same-source codec four-step run and two-plus-two resumed run have identical final parameters. With a constant dev score, the retained best is update1. Resuming latest-continuation.pt into a new directory completes4 updates but never writes weights.safetensors because no new score beats the old best; load_trained then raises KeyError for the missing file.
necessary.impact: A complete resumed training receipt can be unusable for inference and the latest checkpoint does not by itself preserve the best model state required by the frozen earlier-checkpoint tie rule.
necessary.required: Retain a SHA-bound best-state/artifact in the complete continuation protocol and re-export it on resume, or require and verify the complete accompanying best-artifact bundle before any resume updates. Never report a complete export without its selected weights, and do not reset best-selection history to hide the missing state.
